Build global connections, open yourself up to a new world perspective and develop your career prospects. Find out more about what you can achieve abroad with Strathclyde here. Coming to Strathclyde If you're a student currently registered on an undergraduate degree elsewhere in the world then you're able to spend a year (or a semester) of your studies as a visiting student at the University of Strathclyde. You can apply through organised student exchange programmes, which Strathclyde runs in collaboration with more than 250 universities and colleges around the world. Another option is applying directly to Strathclyde on an independent basis, or through a study abroad provider. Get more information on how you can come to Strathclyde to study. Contact Exchange Team Recruitment and International Office Level 7, Room 701 Learning & Teaching Building For Strathclyde students: outgoing-exchanges@strath.ac.uk For Incoming Exchange students: incoming.exchanges@strath.ac.uk Sign up to our newsletter to find out more about studying abroad. Strathclyde Business School Exchange Strathclyde Business School has its own Exchange Team. SBS students should contact the SBS Exchange Team direct for further guidance on available opportunities. Email - sbs-exchange-outgoing@strath.ac.uk Learn more about going on exchange as a Strathclyde Business School student . Go Global Photo Competition Winners 2025 Hamood Al-Harthi - Colegio Iberico Salamanca Spanish Summer School. " Musical show on the river. Salamanca people are known for their love of music. Thus they started to be creative on how they play it, as the photo shown (playing piano on the river)." David Hunter - Semester Exchange at BI Norwegian Business School. "Midnight Sun. Just before summer I road-tripped through Norway's Lofoten Islands above the arctic circle. At this time of year the sun never sets, and our hikes were bound by weather not daylight. It was such a unique experience." Isla Kennedy - Full Year Exchange at Universidad Europea de Madrid. "San Isidro en Madrid. This is the most important festival of Madrid, taking place on the 24th of May. Pictured here are a group of friends in festival dress on their way to street parties." Luke Charles - Full Year Exchange at the University of Oslo. "Norwegian picnic - lunch at the top of Ryten mountain before descending to Kvalvika beach." Use the links on this page whether you are an employee using Self Service, a line manager or department admin completing HR/Payroll processes in Core iTrent or if you’re looking for help and guidance with using iTrent. iTrent Employee Self Service for all staff Use Employee Self Service to: view and download payslips book annual leave purchase additional annual leave (during the annual purchase window) request other types of leave such as time off for medical and dental appointments submit timesheet claims for overtime, hourly fee or fixed fee payments view and update your personal details complete your Performance, Contribution and Development (PCAD) Annual Review Employee self-service Core iTrent for Line Managers & Department Administrators Core iTrent is used to complete manager-led HR processes. Line managers can initiate and progress actions/tasks for their teams, and department administrators can support line managers by preparing information and helping to keep processes moving. This is what you use to log into your emails and other University systems. If you're logging in for the first time from a new device, you will need Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) to access your account. Please see the Information Services Quick Guide if you need help accessing your account. iTrent Resource Centre The iTrent Resource Centre sits on our People Hub. University governance The University of Strathclyde was established by Royal Charter in 1964, with a history dating back to 1796 and the founding of Anderson's Institute. The Charter sets out the power and functions of the University as well as identifying the key officers and committees within the University's structure. Governing Instruments The constitution and governance of the University of Strathclyde is regulated by the Charter, Statutes, Ordinances and Regulations. Committees The University's committee structures are an essential part of the formal decision making process at Strathclyde. Our committee structure is made up of Court, Senate, Executive Team, Strategic Committees and Compliance Committees.
